name: Workload Resource Efficiency
description: Application resource use compared with configured requests and limits.

display.name: Understand usage, requests, and limits
display.description: These values describe containers, not the total memory or CPU use of a VM or physical server.

spec.text: **Usage, requests and limits are different.** Usage is measured consumption. A request reserves scheduling capacity; a limit caps a container. CPU uses mCPU: 1000 mCPU = 1 CPU core. Missing-setting counts count each running Pod once if any regular container lacks that setting. See the list below for the affected Pods and namespaces. Init containers and Pod overhead are excluded.

display.name: CPU used · five busiest pods · mCPU
display.description:
The five pods with highest absolute CPU usage at the end of the selected period are selected once. The chart shows their measured five-minute-average usage over time. This is a consumption ranking, separate from the list above 80% of limits. 1000 mCPU means one CPU core.

When to investigate / alert coverage: CPU Throttling (native)

spec.query: (max by (sre_series) (label_join((sum by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name,container) (avg_over_time(container_cpu_usage{cluster_name=~"${workload_cluster}",namespace=~"${workload_namespace}"}[5m])) / 1000000)), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "pod_name"))) and on (sre_series) (max by (sre_series) (label_join((topk(5, sum by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name) (max by (cluster_name,namespace,pod_name,container) (avg_over_time(container_cpu_usage{cluster_name=~"${workload_cluster}",namespace=~"${workload_namespace}"}[5m] @ end())) / 1000000))), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "namespace", "pod_name")))

display.name: Pods with missing settings · current list

One row per pod and missing setting: cluster, namespace, pod, and setting. The same pod may lack both CPU and memory settings. Counts above deduplicate within each category. Empty means no matching rows; check inventory coverage and filters. This checks running regular containers, not init containers, stopped pods, or optional pod-level resource budgets.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Operational context: no standalone alert; compare with the related error, latency, capacity or collection monitor

This is a compact status list, not a trend. Read the names below; expand + more if needed. Open the linked query and select Table view for separate columns. The link carries cluster/namespace filters but opens the current Metrics Explorer period; reselect a historical period when investigating the past.
